result.summary: Adds a `ReachabilityGoal` tracking framework to fuzz test utilities and instruments 10 fuzz targets. Goals are registered at initialization and tracked across all inputs, failing at exit when `FUZZ_ENFORCE_REACHABILITY=1` if any goal was never reached.
result.problem: Fuzz targets running against static corpora can silently lose coverage of critical paths due to harness or corpus changes without triggering explicit failures.

open_concerns: Author planned an update to validation_load_mempool.cpp to assert coverage of specific mempool features beyond basic load success
resolved_concerns: Switched from lazy registration to an explicit two-phase register/observe pattern to avoid missing goals on early returns
Addressed comment formatting and Mutex annotations in reachability utilities
Clarified purpose of exit code handling at shutdown for corpus replay CI

categories.evidence: Adds reachability tracking utilities under src/test/fuzz/util/ and instruments multiple fuzz harnesses.
categories.rationale: P3 because it provides a reliable harness capability to detect when fuzz corpora silently lose coverage of critical paths like mempool acceptance or P2P handshakes. maflcko noted its utility for corpus CI replay ('mostly for a nightly CI job on a static corpora folder with -runs=1 ... to detect lost path coverage').

result.card: Adds a corpus reachability tracking utility (`ReachabilityGoal`) and instruments 10 fuzz targets with assertions for critical code paths such as mempool acceptance and P2P handshakes. When run with `FUZZ_ENFORCE_REACHABILITY=1`, the target process exits with an error if any registered goal remains unvisited, preventing silent coverage loss in corpus replay CI. The PR has strong support, including an approval from maflcko and concept ACKs from brunoerg and nervana21. Code is ready for review with minor target goal enhancements pending from the author.
